bio.text: Stephen F. Lynch has represented Massachusetts in the U.S. House since he was first sworn in in October 2001, following the death of Rep. John Joseph Moakley.
Lynch grew up in public housing in South Boston, worked as a structural ironworker for 18 years, and joined Boston's Ironworkers Local 7 and was elected president of the union.

He holds a bachelor's degree in construction management from Wentworth Institute of Technology, a law degree from Boston College Law School and a master's in public administration from Harvard's Kennedy School.
Before Congress he served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives, elected in 1994, and then the Massachusetts Senate; he lives in South Boston.
